verses.1: For this reason I judged it necessary for myself not to come again to you in sorrow.
verses.2: For if I grieve you, who is the one who brings me joy if not the one who is grieved because of me?
verses.3: And I wrote the same thing, so that when I come I may not be grieved by those I need to rejoice over, trusting in all of you that my joy is all of yours.
verses.4: For I have written to you out of great affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears, not to grieve you but so that you may know the greater love I have for you.
verses.5: Now if someone has grieved, they have not grieved me, but in part, so as not to burden all of you.
verses.6: This punishment from the majority is enough,
verses.7: so that rather you should forgive and comfort him, or he may be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
verses.8: Therefore I urge you to show him love.
verses.9: For this is why I also wrote, so that you may know the test of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
verses.10: And whatever you forgive, I also forgive. For indeed if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
verses.11: so that we may not be outwitted by Satan, for we do not remain ignorant of his intentions.
verses.12: For when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ and the door was opened to me by the Lord,
verses.13: I had no comfort in my spirit, because I could not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went to Macedonia.
verses.14: Now to the God of all grace, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and who spreads abroad the fragrance of the knowledge of Him everywhere,
verses.15: for we are the fragrance of Christ to God, both to those being saved and to those perishing—
verses.16: to the one group a fragrance of death leading to death, to the other a fragrance of life leading to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
verses.17: For we are not like so many who trade in the word of God, but as from sincerity, and as from God, in Christ we speak before God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "in the presence of Christ" — The phrase ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ is rendered as "in the presence of Christ," following the sense of representing Christ's authority.
raw:
[1] For this reason I judged it necessary for myself not to come again to you in sorrow.
[2] For if I grieve you, who is the one who brings me joy if not the one who is grieved because of me?
[3] And I wrote the same thing, so that when I come I may not be grieved by those I need to rejoice over, trusting in all of you that my joy is all of yours.
[4] For I have written to you out of great affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears, not to grieve you but so that you may know the greater love I have for you.
[5] Now if someone has grieved, they have not grieved me, but in part, so as not to burden all of you.
[6] This punishment from the majority is enough,
[7] so that rather you should forgive and comfort him, or he may be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
[8] Therefore I urge you to show him love.
[9] For this is why I also wrote, so that you may know the test of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
[10] And whatever you forgive, I also forgive. For indeed if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
[11] so that we may not be outwitted by Satan, for we do not remain ignorant of his intentions.
[12] For when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ and the door was opened to me by the Lord,
[13] I had no comfort in my spirit, because I could not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went to Macedonia.
[14] Now to the God of all grace, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and who spreads abroad the fragrance of the knowledge of Him everywhere,
[15] for we are the fragrance of Christ to God, both to those being saved and to those perishing—
[16] to the one group a fragrance of death leading to death, to the other a fragrance of life leading to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
[17] For we are not like so many who trade in the word of God, but as from sincerity, and as from God, in Christ we speak before God.

- v. 10: "in the presence of Christ" — The phrase ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ is rendered as "in the presence of Christ," following the sense of representing Christ's authority.
